title: Invasive plant Control, Okeechobee NWR, FL
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products and commercial services prepared in accordance with the format in Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is issuing a Request for Quotes for the Invasive plant Control at the Okeechobee NWR, FL. The anticipated performance period is shown below. Period of Performance: Contract award to September 30, 2027 Solicitation 140FF027Q0084 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) is 100% Small Business Set Aside and is conducted under FAR Parts 12 and 13, incorporating provisions and clauses in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC Number: 2026-01, Effective Date: 03/13/2026. The applicable North American Classification System (NAICS) code is 115310, Support Activities for Forestry. The small business size standard is $11.5 Million. Terms & Conditions: Any additional contract requirement(s) or terms and conditions determined by the contracting officer to be necessary for this acquisition and consistent with customary commercial practices are attached included in the Attachment Solicitation-provisions and clauses- 140FF027Q0084. The full text of the referenced FAR clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/far/ or see terms & conditions attached to the solicitation. In order to be eligible for award, all contractors must have an Active Registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) website https://sam.gov/content/home. Please note, SAM is a free website and there is never a cost to register your entity. Prior to or following receipt of an award, the Contractor must register with the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Invoice Processing Platform System (IPP) to submit requests for payment. Please note, IPP is a free website and there is never a cost to complete registration. Invoices for services will be paid after the end of the month of service, advanced payments are not allowed. Instructions For all Instructions to Offerors please reference Attachments 1-4. Important Submission Dates & Site Visit Info: 1. Site Inspection: Prior to submitting a quote, offerors or quoters are urged and expected to inspect the site where services are to be performed and to satisfy themselves regarding all general and local conditions that may affect the cost of contract performance. A site visit can be scheduled by contacting the technical point of contact. Please contact the Refuge POC Oliver Van Den Ende at oliver_vanenende@fws.gov, 772-205-0697 to arrange a site visit. 2. Question Submission: All questions regarding this Solicitation must be submitted in writing to the Contract Specialist, Fred Riley at Fred_riley@ios.doi.gov no later than Friday, November 27, 2026, at 2:00pm EDT. If necessary, questions received will be answered through an Amendment to this Solicitation. Emails must indicate the following in the subject line: Question Submission for 140FF027Q0084. 3. Quote Submission: Quotes (including all required documents) must be transmitted via e-mail to the Contract Specialist, Fred Riley at fred_riley@ios.doi.gov, no later than Monday, November 30, 2026, at 2:00pm EDT. Emails must indicate the following in the subject line: Quote Submission 140 FF027Q0084 Required Submittal Documents: Offerors responding to this solicitation must submit the following documents: - See Attachment 1- Solicitation- provisions_and_clauses-_FF027Q0084- ADDENDUM TO 52.212-1, INSTRUCTIONS TO OFFERORS Complete the attached document or your own version that addresses each element. Your quote will be considered non-responsive and will not be considered if all the above required documents are not completed in full and received as part of your submittal package. An award will be made to the Contractor whose submittal documents conform to the requirements as described in this solicitation and who, based on a subjective assessment from the Government, offers the best value to include technical, past experience, and price. The Government reserves the right to award a contract to other than the lowest priced offer if, in its judgment, the non-cost factors outweighs the price difference. CONTRACT DOCUMENTS, EXHIBITS, OR ATTACHMENTS See attached documents: ATTACHMENT 1 Performance Work Statement ATTACHMENT 2 Quote Schedule ATTACHMENT 3 SCA Wage Determination ATTACHMENT 4 Past Performance Questionnaire Contracting Officer/Office: Fred Riley, Contract Specialist U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service Hadley, MA Joint Administrative Operations (JAO) fred_riley@ios.doi.gov

title: HANGAR 140 RENOVATIONS AT NAVAL AIR STATON (NAS) JACKSONVILLE (JAX), JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA
description: The H140 Renovations project scope encompasses the entire 111,000 SF facility, including the Administration, Shops, and Maintenance wings (O1 and O2 spaces) as well as the Organizational Hangar (OH space). The O spaces will include space reconfiguration and replacement of finishes, ceiling systems, lighting and plumbing fixtures. Work also includes replacement of the sliding steel hangar bay doors. Building envelope work will replace the high-bay clerestory windows with high-efficiency thermal windows and provide repair or replacement of walls, cladding, windows, doors. Roofing systems over the hangar high bay, and administration wings will be replaced, while exterior envelope rehabilitation will address hazardous material removal, concrete and masonry repair, and sealing and recoating of surfaces. Replaced building envelope components will be designed to achieve hurricane resistance, Anti-Terrorism Force Protection compliance, and weather-tight performance, but do not entail modifications to the structure. Also included to replace three bridge cranes, two 5 Ton and one 2 Ton. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 945 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $50,000,000 and $100,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this solicitation is 236210 � Industrial Building Construction, PSC Z2JZ - Repair or Alteration of Miscellaneous Buildings with a Small Business Size Standard of $45 million (M). Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 15 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The anticipated award date is Fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-6). Complete submission package shall not exceed 4 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.), if applicable for NAICS Code 236210 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number). 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6.) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7.) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of three (3) projects including contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, project completion dates, performance ratings, and evidence of specific capabilities listed below: Demonstrate Prime Contractor experience constructing or repairing an industrial facility that was self-performed. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at approximately $50 million or greater, similar in size, scope and complexity to the proposed hangar repairs and completed and accredited/certified within the past five (5) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including completion date and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. After completing its analysis, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among 8(a), HubZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, and/or Small Business firms or to proceed with issuing an unrestricted solicitation, inviting full and open competition. Please respond to this announcement no later than 30 November 2026, NLT 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time via email to Delcheia Turner, Delcheia.l.turner.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson, aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: HANGAR 140 RENOVATIONS AT NAS JAX, FL. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

description: This is a Small Business Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for quote. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified small business sources to perform a potential R&D requirement. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified small business sources technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. Background: This project seeks to design and test spray suitable for phage hygiene products formulation for the prevention of UTI that maintain activity under extreme thermal conditions. Once a spray formula is identified and passes all necessary testing, prototype spray devices will be assembled for testing. The requesting organization has identified a phage cocktail having suitable activity and stability in lab-based solutions. The requesting organization has test potential formulation components used for topical skin applications for maintenance of titer and stability. Various components include phage storage buffer solutions, preservatives, potentiators, emollients, humectants and other additives utilized cosmetic products. "In accordance with FAR 37.104(a), this requirement does not constitute a personal services contract as it does not create an employer-employee relationship. All tasks will be executed independently by the contractor, and the Government will not exercise direct supervision or control over contractor personnel.�. Purpose/Objective: This request is to conduct the development, safety testing, and production of custom prototype bacteriophage hygiene sprays designed for intimate skin applications to target UTI-causing E. coli. The Contractor shall design, develop and test a phage friendly formulation for prototype cosmetic phage hygiene sprays. Phage formulation properties will include maintenance of thermal stability and possess suitable properties for manufacture of prototype cosmetic products. Components must not inhibit or otherwise reduce phage titer during storage, including at elevated temperature (45oC) for 4 weeks. Project Requirements: Standard topical cosmetic manufacturers lack the biological expertise to handle live phages, while traditional phage laboratories do not possess the cosmetic-adjacent formulation infrastructure for sensitive skin areas. Contractors are sought that should have previous experience working with phage for cosmetic products, including making prototypes and formulation development for thermal stability needed for product storage at elevated temperatures that meet cosmetic regulatory requirements. The Contractor shall provide project management support for the overall administration of the contract and development, tracking, and management of all task orders issued under the contract. The Contractor�s support staff shall work in coordination with designated federal staff and be responsible for performing all the non-inherently governmental activities associated with administration of this contract. Task Area 1: Formula development & optimization The contractor shall independently formulate and deliver three (3) formulation iterations incorporating provided phage cocktail. The contractor shall independently analyze this data to determine and execute subsequent formulation adjustments, leveraging its proprietary prototyping expertise to deliver the next physical iteration. Following the delivery of each iteration prototype, the requesting organization will provide data of the formulation effect on Phage thermal stability/titer and determination of formulation suitability for potential inclusion into prototype sprays. Iteration 1 will be formulated by the contractor using previous data generated by the requesting organization and will be sent to requestor for evaluations/ assessment. The requestor will return the results of Phage cocktail thermal stability/titer thermal stability data to contractor. Iteration 2 will be developed after the contractor receives the assessment results for iteration 1. The contractor will assess the results to inform adjustments/changes to the spray formulation composition to improve/ maintain phage cocktail thermal stability/titer at 45oC storage. This may involve adjusting formulation concentrations or substituting alternatives components within the limitations described by the requestor. This iteration will be sent to the requestor for evaluations/ assessment of Phage cocktail thermal stability/titer. Iteration 3 will be developed by the contractor after receiving the results of the iteration 2 evaluations. The contractor will assess the results to inform adjustments/changes to the spray formulation composition to maintain/ improve phage cocktail thermal stability/titer at 45oC storage. This may involve adjusting formulation concentrations or substituting alternatives components within the limitations described by the requestor. This iteration will be sent to the requestor for evaluation/ of stability properties as the final formulation. Formulation Testing: Formulation components will be combined and assessed for: 1) thermal stability (3-cycle freeze/thaw testing and accelerated heat stability testing); 2) preservative challenge test; and 3) Human Repeated Insult Path Test (HRIPT).Task Area 2: Prototype production � Once formulation is finalized, prototype spray bottles will be made containing phage cocktail in optimized formulation, and formulation only (no phage).: Optimized formulation that maintains thermal stability and suitable for prototype cosmetic sprays. Components include phage cocktail (concentration >1E8 PFU/ml), phage buffer (pH 7 to 7.5), stabilizer(s), preservative(s)/enhancer, moisturizer(s) (humectants/emollients). Number of units: 50 bottles with phage cocktail in optimized formulation, 50 bottles containing formulation only. Prototypes delivered to requestor overnight on ice or ice packs. Spray bottle volume: 15 ml (0.5 oz), with 14 ml solution. Spray bottles must have fine mist pump delivery (70 � 150 ul). Spray bottles must have 360-degree delivery (including when sprayed upside down) Spray bottle material: opaque plastic (HDPE). Spray bottle caps and neck to be sealed with heat-shrunk plastic. Spray bottles to be labeled numerically 1 to 50 (for formulation only, no phage) and 51 to 100 (for phage cocktail in optimized formulation). Package spray bottles numbered 1-50 separately from bottles numbered 51-100. Use cardboard boxes with dividers to keep the bottles protected and separated. The contractor will purchase suitable spray bottles. Regulatory process: Establish that the product meets Modernization of Cosmetic Regulation Act Compliance (MoCRA) specifications: Preservative Challenge Testing: ensures the product remains free from bacterial, yeast and mold contamination during storage. Ingredients Toxicity Study: A safety assessment to determine the toxicity of individual ingredients in the formula based on published studies and safety assessments in cosmetic products. The prototypes from this procurement will be evaluated in a user acceptability study by female Warfighters. Capability statement /information sought. Respondents must provide clear and convincing documentation of their capability of providing the manufacturing and studies support services specified in this notice. title: Hubble Space Telescope (HST) Servicing
description: THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. NO PROPOSALS ARE TO BE SUBMITTED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. This notice is issued by the NASA/Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) to post a Request for Information to solicit responses from interested parties. This document is for information and planning purposes and to allow industry the opportunity to verify reasonableness and feasibility of the requirement, as well as promote competition. Background: The Hubble Space Telescope (HST) remains a top astrophysical research facility in high demand (over 7:1 oversubscription) with 1000+ scientific papers a year (and growing), complementing the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), the Roman Space Telescope (RST), and other observatories, with no replacement expected before ~2040. Hubble�s unique UV/optical capabilities provide critical insights across the entire field of astrophysics, including solar system dynamics, the formation of other planetary systems, exoplanet atmospheres, cataclysmic phenomena throughout the universe, temperature and chemistry throughout and between galaxies, the life cycles of stars and evolution of galaxies. Extending the scientific life of HST will extend the availability of its unique capabilities until the potential replacement, Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO), is operational. In addition, an on-orbit servicing activity to enhance the performance of the observatory or increase its resilience to the effects of aging will help minimize or eliminate the time gap between the existence of the HST capabilities and those of HWO. Lifetime analysis performed in July 2026 identified a 10% probability of reentry by September 2032, and 50% probability by December 2033. HST does not have a propulsion system and, without a servicing action, will ultimately experience an uncontrolled reentry. Mission Options NASA/ Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) is hereby soliciting information from potential sources for a potential requirement for orbital altitude increase, on-orbit servicing, and/or orbital disposal or controlled reentry for the Hubble Space Telescope (HST). Information is sought about current and near-term capabilities to perform one or more of the following mission options: Develop, test, and operate a servicing vehicle capable of capturing the HST in low earth orbit and boosting it to at least 600 km Develop, test, and operate a servicing mission to HST to enhance its ongoing performance and increase its resilience and expected on-orbit lifetime Develop, test, and operate a mission to HST to perform a controlled reentry disposal. The requirement includes that the boost and/or servicing mission must not harm the HST and that this mission is expected to occur by 2032. GSFC would provide technical information about the HST, technical consultation with GSFC HST experts, and coordinated HST operations to facilitate rendezvous, capture, boost, servicing, and/or controlled reentry. The contractor would be expected to provide all other resources (including the launch vehicle, spacecraft, crew if applicable, and servicing vehicle mission operations) to successfully perform the mission. This RFI is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government, nor will the Government pay for the information submitted in response. The Government may not respond to questions/concerns submitted. The Government will use the information to finalize the RFP as necessary. RESPONSES As part of your response, please indicate your level of interest in responding to a potential solicitation for this requirement. Interested offerors shall address any or all mission options stated above with the following requirements. Your response should include, at a minimum: Describe your ability to fully perform the mission option(s). Responses should include: Name of submitter and contact information (institutional affiliation, E-mail address). Description of your ability to fully perform any or all mission options stated above Description of your current level of experience or qualifications for each mission option by providing objective evidence of that experience or qualifications (specific but brief examples that clearly indicate the specific experience or qualifications). If you are unable to fully perform an activity, identify such is the case, and address how you may accommodate the area(s) that you cannot currently perform. The technical objectives of the envisioned demonstration. Description of the concept of operations and timeline for mission concept and completion Technical approach(es) for launch, rendezvous with and capture of HST and the current technology readiness level (TRL) of key components, Length of period docked with HST Control of the combined vehicle stack If boosting, amount of boost expected to be obtained, and the minimum altitude of HST that the service can be performed to achieve a boost to at least 600 km An assessment of the mission risk and risk to HST and risk mitigation measures. The earliest date you will be able to perform the service, The maximum HST body rates that can be accommodated during capture. An estimate of cost, payment schedule, and assumptions about your access to government facilities. A description of the monetary and non-monetary contributions/resources the respondent expects to need from NASA. A list of potential partners, including international partners, if any. Your business size and socioeconomic status under applicable NAICS codes. Respondents are requested to provide informed input on realistic and appropriate SB subcontracting and/or participation goals for the specific requirement. This type of feedback supports NASA�s market research and helps ensure the acquisition strategy is aligned with actual industry capability. Industry feedback is requested for: SB Subcontracting goals; Barriers that may limit SB participation, such as certifications, unique technical requirements, security needs, specialized tools, or high-risk performance areas and/or Strategies to increase SB participation, including: Breaking requirements into smaller components Identifying areas appropriate for subcontracting Considering teaming or mentor prot�g� approaches All comments or questions must be submitted electronically via email to Raymond Jones at Raymond.R.Jones@nasa.gov, no later than November 30, 2026 at 3 p.m. eastern standard time (EST). When responding reference 80GSFC27RFIHSTS. All responses should be submitted as a PDF file, 12-point Times New Roman font where paragraphed, as well as single spaced pages with one-inch margins, No more than 25 pages in length.. Files should not be password protected. Respondents may not submit export-controlled information, including International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) restricted information, in response to this RFI. If a respondent submits confidential and/or proprietary information in its response to this RFI, the respondent must clearly mark the information accordingly. Because the purpose of this RFI is to gain awareness of commercial capabilities to boost on-orbit satellites, if a respondent chooses to submit confidential or proprietary information, the respondent agrees that the Government may use that information for future planning purposes. Any public discussion of the results of this RFI may disclose information about the identities of the respondents. NASA Clause 1852.215-84, Ombudsman, is applicable. The Center Ombudsman for this acquisition can be found at: https://www.hq.nasa.gov/office/procurement/regs/Procurement-Ombuds-Comp-Advocate-Listing.pdf If a solicitation is released, then it and any additional documents will be available on Sam.gov. It is the offeror's responsibility to monitor this website for the release of the solicitation and amendments (if any). Potential offerors will be responsible for downloading their own copy of the solicitation and amendments, if any.

description: SOLICITATION SPE603-26-R-0543 Government-Owned, Contactor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor-Owned/Contractor-Operated (COCO) fuel services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center 29 Palms, CA Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) - Energy - FESAB is issuing a Request for Proposal (RFP) for Government-Owned, Contractor-Operated (GOCO) and Contractor Owned, Contractor-Operated (COCO) Fuel Storage, Operations, and Distribution services at Marine Corps Air Ground Combat Center (MCAGCC) 29 Palms, CA. title: Experimental and Mathematical Biomechanics Injury Research IDIQ
description: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is committed to saving lives, preventing injuries, and reducing traffic-related health care and economic costs. As part of that mission, the Office of Vehicle Safety Research (OVSR) supports a robust scientific research program to provide the technical foundation for NHTSA�s vehicle and traffic safety initiatives. This procurement seeks to establish an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to support NHTSA�s Experimental and Mathematical Biomechanics Injury Research (EMBIR) program. The IDIQ will enable the issuance of Task Orders (TOs) that require a broad range of specialized research, analysis, and technical support services related to human injury mechanisms and prevention in motor vehicle crashes. The contractor shall provide services across the following four research domains: Experimental Biomechanics: Conduct physical testing to evaluate human injury tolerance under crashrelevant loading conditions and identify the mechanisms and thresholds for injury. 1.Anthropomorphic Test Device (ATD) Support: Provide technical expertise to develop and assess ATDs, ensuring biofidelity, durability, and measurement accuracy. 2.Computational Modeling: Develop and utilize advanced computational models (e.g., finite element models of the human body and ATDs) to simulate crash scenarios, validate injury mechanisms, and support virtual testing environments. 3.Crash and Injury Data Analysis: Analyze real-world crash data, ATD testing, and experimental research to support injury criteria development, identify emerging crash trends, and enhance vehicle safety metrics. Data science tools such as AI/machine learning may be applied to enhance insights from large-scale datasets.

title: Q519--Research Support Psychological Assessment for PTSD Clinical Trial
description: This is not a solicitation. The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to award a sole source contract to Precision Psychological Assessments, LLC, located at 2 Ironworks Circle, Ivyland, PA 18974, for a base period and two (2) option periods to obtain gold-standard psychological diagnostic assessments conducted within the context of a multi-site PTSD clinical research trial in support of the study entitled Hybrid Implementation and Non-Inferiority Testing of Group Versus Individual Written Exposure Therapy (WET) for Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Based on market research conducted by the Government, including a Sources Sought Notice, the Government identified Precision Psychological Assessments, LLC as the only source that demonstrated an existing operational capability to provide independent PTSD clinical research assessments utilizing trained CAPS-5 and MINI evaluators, established assessment fidelity monitoring processes, ongoing rater calibration and reliability review procedures, doctoral-level PTSD assessment oversight, and multi-site clinical trial assessment support. Because the assessments serve as a primary outcome measure for the study, the Government requires an established assessment infrastructure capable of supporting consistent, blinded, and standardized assessments throughout the period of performance. Performance requires more than access to licensed mental health professionals. The contractor must maintain an established pool of trained independent raters; provide senior doctoral-level oversight; ensure evaluator availability across multiple sites and time zones; conduct standardized training, calibration, fidelity monitoring, and inter-rater reliability reviews; maintain research and regulatory compliance; and provide continuity of assessment services throughout the clinical trial. The Government determined that reliance on future staffing, evaluator certification, or proposed teaming arrangements would introduce unacceptable risk to assessment continuity, assessment fidelity, inter-rater reliability, and protocol compliance for the study's primary outcome measures. Accordingly, the Government identified Precision Psychological Assessments, LLC as the only source that demonstrated an existing operational capability to satisfy these requirements. Responses to this Notice Since the intent is to procure these services on a sole-source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities on SAM.gov. The applicable NAICS Code is 541990, All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services, with a size standard of $19.5 million. The applicable PSC is Q519. Interested parties may submit information demonstrating their capability to meet the Government's requirement. title: NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE
description: The United States Special Operations Command (USSOCOM), on behalf of the SOCOM J2X Directorate, hereby gives notice of its intent to negotiate and award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price purchase order/contract to: 360 Defense 7533 S Center View Ct, Ste N West Jordan, UT 84084 This procurement is conducted under the authority of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13, Simplified Acquisition Procedures, specifically: FAR 13.106-1(b)(1): Soliciting from a single source for purchases not exceeding the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) when the Contracting Officer determines that the circumstances of the contract action deem only one source reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, or brand-name/proprietary compatibility). FAR Part 12: Acquisition of Commercial Products and Commercial Services The requiring activity (USSOCOM J2X) requires the acquisition of tactical monitoring and surveillance hardware components: 10/ea Sentinel Pro with Controller (Integrated tactical surveillance sensor/payload and matching handheld command controller unit) 360 Defense is the sole designer, original equipment manufacturer (OEM), and proprietary distributor of the Sentinel Pro system and its associated tactical command controllers. Key technical and operational factors supporting this sole-source action include: Proprietary Hardware & Firmware Architecture: The Sentinel Pro utilizes proprietary hardware interfaces, secured datalinks, and specialized command firmware that are solely manufactured and serviced by 360 Defense. No third-party commercial vendor holds authorized manufacturing or distribution rights. Interoperability & Standardization: SOCOM J2X operational workflows require equipment that integrates directly into existing tactical architecture without latency or cross-platform data corruption. Introducing non-compatible alternative hardware would require redesign of mounting systems, auxiliary cabling, operator re-qualification, and software recertification at significant duplicated expense and substantial operational downtime. No Authorized Resellers: Market research conducted by the requiring activity confirmed that 360 Defense does not utilize third-party distributors or value-added resellers for this specific platform configuration. THIS IS NOT A FORMAL REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS. A solicitation package will not be posted publicly. However, in accordance with FAR 5.207 and FAR 13.106-1(b)(1), any interested party that believes it can satisfy this requirement with a fully compliant, interoperable alternative is invited to submit a written capabilities statement. All capability statements must demonstrate: Clear technical evidence that the offered platform meets or exceeds all technical, physical, and firmware specifications of the Sentinel Pro with Controller. Proof of authorized manufacturing/distribution rights or direct compatibility without technical or firmware modifications. Pricing structure, delivery schedule, and Cage Code / Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) registered in SAM.gov. Submission Instructions: Format: Electronic submission via PDF (max 5 pages) A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer. title: F--A34 STOCKPILE REMOVAL
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS FOR A34 Stockpile Removal The Bureau of Reclamation, Interior Region 8: Lower Colorado Basin (LCB), Yuma Area Office (YAO), is seeking sources to collect, haul, and dispose of all material from the designated stockpile, which includes asbestos cement pipe (ACP), to an appropriate waste facility. Contractor will provide certified personnel to verify complete ACP removal at the site. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS, QUOTE, OR AN INVITATION FOR BIDS and does not constitute any commitment by the Government. No formal solicitation for this work exists at this time. All qualified concerns may submit capability statements for consideration. Capability statements received will be reviewed to determine the technical, administrative, and management capability of such offerors to perform this type of work. The capability statements will be used to determine the appropriate procurement strategy whether a set-aside or an alternate procurement strategy is warranted. The Government does not intend to award a contract and will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. All interested sources must respond to future solicitation announcements separately from responses to the sources sought notice. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this project is 562910, Remediation Services, Small Business Standard Size 1,000 in number of employees. All interested parties should verify that they fall under the NAICS code as a Small Business prior to submission. Responses to this notice will be used by the Government to make the appropriate acquisition decision. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM.gov). BACKGROUND: The Bureau of Reclamation (BOR), Lower Colorado Basin, Yuma Area Office (YAO), has a requirement to remove and properly dispose of debris and materials contained within a designated stockpile area. The work includes over-excavation and disposal of the top 8 inches of soil beneath the stockpile, followed by post-removal soil sampling to verify that asbestos contamination is no longer present. If asbestos concentrations exceeding background levels are identified during verification sampling, the Contractor shall perform additional excavation and disposal only to the extent necessary to achieve acceptable levels. Protecting the health and safety of all personnel involved in the work is of paramount importance. BOR owns property in Yuma County, Arizona, containing fragments of broken asbestos-cement pipe (ACP). The site has historically been used as a gravel stockpile yard that supports YAO water system facilities. Under this requirement, the Contractor shall collect, transport, and legally dispose of all material within the designated stockpile area, including ACP, at an approved disposal facility. The Contractor shall provide qualified and certified personnel to verify complete ACP removal and compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, transportation, supervision, and incidentals necessary to perform the work in a safe and satisfactory manner. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The Government anticipates the term of the contract shall be 180 calendar days from the date of receipt of a Notice-of-Award. NORMAL PERFORMANCE HOURS: Services are to be performed in accordance with the Statement Of Work (SOW) between the hours of 6:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. (PT), Monday through Friday, holidays excluded. Contractor shall notify government representatives when accessing the site for both normal and after hours. Gate shall remain closed and locked after departure. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: - The abatement work required is located on BOR property along the Salinity Canal in Yuma County, AZ. Major cross streets are S Avenue 4-1/2E and E Levee Rd. Refer to the Project Location Map included in the Appendix Part C. Contractor is allowed to stage within the fenced stockpile yard and daisy chain a lock on the gate. Contractor shall: not obstruct Reclamation maintenance staff from continuing work activities within the yard. SMALL BUSINESS CERTIFICATION WITH THE SMALL BUSINESS ADMINISTRATION (SBA): The Government is only interested in responses from small businesses that can perform the services. Please identify your federally designated small business category or categories. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity. Based on the responses to this Sources Sought Notice/Market Research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submission. SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS: All interested and qualified firms responding to this Sources Sought Notice are required to provide the following information: 1. Business Name, physical/mailing address, phone, point of contact, email and website if applicable; 2. Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) Number; 3. Firm's Capability Statement: The Capability Statements shall be no more than 5-pages in length. Please address the particulars of this effort, with appropriate documentation supporting claims of organizational and staff capability; 4. A list of similar projects within the last five (5) years (at least three (3) descriptions) *Note: The list of relevant contracts/projects shall include the location, contract number, description, and estimated yearly value, and performance dates; 5. Any or all Small Business Classifications (Tell us if you are certified with the SBA under a socio-economic program such as, but, not limited to 8(a) Program, SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, Small Disadvantaged, WOSB, ISBEE) 6. Responses should be titled as: 140RR027Q0050 A34 Stockpile Removal SS Response � (Insert Company Name). Interested parties who consider themselves qualified to perform the above listed services are invited to submit a response to this Sources Sought Notice no later than 12:00 p.m. (PS) November 30, 2026. All responses under this Sources Sought Notice must be emailed to Colleen Samuels, Contract Specialist at colleen.samuels@ios.doi.gov. Facsimiles will not be accepted. Oral communications ARE NOT acceptable in response to this notice.

title: Laboratory Capabilities to Test Railroad Tank Car Thermal Protection Systems (TPS)
description: Request for Information (RFI) only. This RFI is amended to extend the response date to 11/30/2026 at 3:00PM EST. Purpose This RFI seeks information regarding Laboratory Capabilities to perform pool and torch fire tests of Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) to the U.S. DOT Volpe Center. A qualified vendor must be capable of performing pool and torch fire tests as described in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B. The vendor should also be capable of performing light fabrication and/or assembly of test specimens for the aforementioned tests. Qualified vendors are requested to respond as detailed further below, which includes capability, small business classification, estimated lead time including any risks that may impact delivery, and any other industry concerns the government might consider before solicitation. The intent is to gather information to inform a possible future procurement or contract. Background The Federal Railroad Administration (FRA) is conducting research into the performance of TPS for railroad tank cars. TPS are designed to delay or prevent the catastrophic release of hazardous materials from a railroad tank car exposed to fires that may result from train derailments. In the FRA�s planned research, test specimens of TPS are to be evaluated in simulated pool fire and torch fire conditions similar to those defined in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. The durations of the fire exposure would extend beyond the 100 minute pool fire and 30 minute torch fire duration specified in Appendix B to 49 CFR 179. Pool fire test specimens are applied to a 1 foot by 1 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. Torch fire test specimens are applied to a 4 foot by 4 foot steel plate of nominal 0.625 inch thickness. The Volpe Center is looking to perform a minimum of two (2) pool fire tests and two (2) torch fire tests for each TPS. The total number of TPS to be tested has not yet been determined. Although the tests will be similar to those defined in 49 CFR 179 Appendix B, this research may require some modifications to the test protocol including but not limited to additional instrumentation, data collection or varying of test parameters such as duration of the fire exposure. The Volpe Center is also looking for the capability to perform light fabrication of test specimens as detailed above. For examples of possible fabrication requirements, see https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/standards-rulemaking/hazmat/tank-car-thermal-protection-system-list Scope of Information Requested The U.S. DOT Volpe Center is seeking information from commercial testing laboratories, university laboratories, and other interested parties on their willingness, ability, and experience in conducting the simulated pool and torch fire testing planned for various tank car TPS. Descriptions of your facility�s pool and torch fire testing capabilities, including equipment, experience, capacity, resources and staff preparedness for testing tank car TPS. You are encouraged to submit publications of relevant past work. Descriptions of any laboratory accreditation or certification related to pool fire testing. Laboratory hourly rates, technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. Descriptions of staff/facility/equipment availability, including any limitations on when fire testing may be conducted (e.g., blackout dates due to seasonal weather conditions) Information on any pre-test data or preliminary sample testing that may be required prior to a full-scale test. Information on your typical post-test laboratory analyses and report formats, and your ability to tailor report/data formats to customer requirements. Description of your facility�s fabrication and assembly capabilities, including: Cutting of 11 gauge steel sheet (0.1196 inches) Cutting of 0.625 inch steel plate Cutting of insulating materials that may generate hazardous airborne particulates such as fiberglass. Mixing and application of coatings to required specifications similar to examples on the PHMSA TPS list. What is the required lead time for fabrication of test specimens? Technical personnel rates, general facility and equipment usage charges, overhead and other expenses, etc. for fabrication of test specimens. Estimated time to conduct one simulated pool fire and one simulated torch fire test including setup, conduct of the test, cooldown, and teardown of test setup. Any other comments that can help the U.S. DOT Volpe Center better define the research scope and direction and ultimately yield technical data beneficial to both the government and industry are welcome. Responses should include the above as well as: Company information Name UEI Address POC information This RFI is for information and planning purposes only and is a market research tool to determine the availability and adequacy of sources prior to determining the method of acquisition and possible issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation for bids, quotations, and proposals, and is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government. The information provided herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to solicit for or award a competitive contract. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary, and the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government.

The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID "is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD." These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. title: Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Service
description: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Keyport is issuing this Request for Quote for Silver Reutilization and Account Maintenance Services. The requirement involves the refinement of silver-bearing material recovered from batteries, for which the refined silver will be used to manufacture new batteries that require silver of 99.9% purity. AnnuaI requirements: Silver Reutilization High Silver Content 380,000 troy ounces | Silver Reutilization Low Silver Content 725,000 troy ounces | Silver Account Maintenance 500,000 troy ounces | Transaction Fee 10 each | Contract Data Requirements List 1 Lot (Not Separately Priced). This Request for Quote is for commercial services and is posted in accordance with FAR Subpart 5.201. The Government intends to award one (1) Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period, using Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) source selection procedures. The contract type will be Firm-Fixed-Price and Fixed-Price with Economic Price Adjustment-Cost Index in accordance with FAR 16.203-4(d). The applicable Product Service Code (PSC) for the requirement is P999 (Salvage - other) and the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 331492 (Secondary Smelting, Refining, and Alloying of nonferrous Metal (except Copper and Aluminum)), with a small business size standard of 850 employees. The Request for Quote is competed using full and open competition simplified procedures under FAR Subpart 12.201. The Request for Quote is available through the Solicitation Module in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) at https://piee.eb.mil/. Interested vendors must establish a PIEE account and obtain Proposal Manager role activation through the PIEE Contractor Administrator to submit offers electronically. Vendors will need a Digital PIN, One-Time Password, and CAGE Code to successfully save and submit offers through the system. For information and instructions regarding the Solicitation Module in PIEE, please visit https://dodprocurementtoolbox.com/site-pages/solicitation-module.Offerors must have a current registration and completed representations and certifications in the System for Award Management (SAM) at https://sam.gov/, a Federal Government owned website. For questions regarding this procurement, contact Christina Schmitt at christina.m.schmitt.civ@us.navy.mil and Robert Fisher at robert.v.fisher.civ@us.navy.mil.

description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE SYNOPSIS: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a sources sought notice only. This is NOT a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of commercially available products that may be of interest to the United States Coast Guard (USCG). The USCG, Aviation Logistics Center is conducting market research to determine repair sources described as follows: BACKGROUND: The USCG operates C-27J Maritime Patrol Aircraft. These Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA) operate differently from general aviation in support of USCG search and rescue missions, as well as surveillance and reconnaissance missions. The USCG C-27J missions require frequent operation at lower altitudes and in salt-laden environments. These environments accelerate corrosion on airframe structures, engines and components of the aircraft. The aircraft and its components are inspected by USCG personnel In Accordance With (IAW) the Original Equipment Manufacturer�s (OEM) periodic requirements and in conjunction with the USCG's specialized Asset Computerized Maintenance System (ACMS). The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of any commercially available vendors that may be of interest to the USCG. This notice is to assist the USCG in determining the potential sources capable of procurement for the services listed below. The Engine OEM is Rolls Royce Corporation who retains proprietary data rights. SERVICES: Field Service Representative services in support of C-27J aircraft. Program Manager/Engineering services in support of C-27 aircraft. REPLIES: Responses to this notice should include company name, address, and telephone number, point of contact (POC), details on company quality systems and include documentation that provides traceability to the OEM for each part, complete product details, brochures, etc., which will allow the USCG to understand your product, configurations, auxiliary equipment and options. Please state the approximate lead-time for acquiring your product and the details and terms of any standard warranty included with the product. Responses can be for all or for a few of the part numbers listed. Please provide the details and terms of any standard warranty included with the product. Please respond to the following questions: (1) Is your business a large or small business and how many employees? (2) If small, does your firm qualify as a small, emergent business, or a small, disadvantaged business? (3) If disadvantaged, specify under which disadvantaged group and is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? (4) Is your firm a certified hub zone firm? (5) Is your firm a woman-owned or operated business? (6) Is your firm a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned? (7) Is your product listed on a GSA schedule? (8) Do you have other government agencies using the product, and if so which agencies, POCs and contract numbers? (9) If possible, any POCs for civilian users for general usage of product questions. After the review of the responses to this sources sought announcement, and if the USCG still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a solicitation announcement will be published on the SAM.GOV website. Insert "70Z03827IW0000008 Response" in the subject line of the email. After review of the responses to this sources sought announcement, and if the USCG decides to proceed with an acquisition, a solicitation announcement will be published on the SAM.GOV website. Again, this is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this sources notice shall be emailed to dane.w.hobbs@uscg.mil. TELEPHONE RESPONSES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Responses must be received no later than 30 November 2026 at 4:00PM EST. Firms responding to this announcement that fail to provide all of the required information cannot be used to help the USCG make the appropriate acquisition decisions which is the intent of this sources sought notice. This notice is to assist the USCG in identifying potential sources only. All firms responding to this sources sought notice are advised that their response to this notice is not a request to be considered for a contract award. All interested parties must respond to any subsequent solicitation announcement separately from the responses to this announcement. Responses to this sources sought notice are NOT a request to be added to a prospective offerors list or to receive a copy of the solicitation. title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: Amendment released on 11/4/2026 for Volume 1 Q&A responses. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. title: Overhaul of the UH-60 POWER TURBINE MODULE
description: The purpose of this Amendment 0004 to solicitation W58RGZ-26-B-0012 is to formally update the acquisition approach and restructure the requirement. The Defense Contract Management Agency (DCMA) Commercial Item Group (CIG) has issued a formal determination concluding that the maintenance and overhaul (M&O) services for the Power Turbine Module of the Black Hawk weapons system described in this solicitation meet the definition of a commercial product/commercial service in accordance with FAR 2.101. Consequently, this solicitation is hereby converted from a noncommercial requirement to a commercial requirement conducted under FAR Part 12. Additionally, this amendment restructures the contract type from a five-year Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to a three-year IDIQ and incorporates mandatory regulatory updates in compliance with the recent Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO).

title: Soft White Wheat
description: The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) is seeking capability statements from all firms interested in a proposed soft white wheat Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) contract to be delivered in Pocatello, ID. Soft White Wheat for the Pocatello Supply Depot are required to meet the following specifications: Product Specifications: Quality Cleaned Food Grade Wheat Moisture 13.25 - 14.00% Protein 9.5 -10.5% Fat 1.0 - 1.7% Total Dietary Fiber 9.0 -13.0% Bushel Test Weight 58 lbs./bu* *Post cleaning Total Defects Not to exceed 2.3 gm/lb. Defects Include � Dockage � Non-wheat grains {such as barley, rye, corn, seeds, etc.) � Damaged wheat {insect bored, weather, ground heat, mold, frost damaged, etc.) � Shrunken and broken kernels which pass a 0.634 3/8 oblong hole sieve according to FGIS procedure. � Insect bored kernels limited to 3/16 � Foreign material - all non-wheat material which remains on the screen in the dockage machine. � Zero tolerance for injurious materials such as metal, glass, rodent pellets, etc. � Zero tolerance for garlic. Packaging: Soft White Wheat will be bagged in 50 lb. bags and stacked 40 bags to a pallet. Bags will be neatly stacked on pallets and wrapped to prevent shifting. All interested parties are invited to submit complete the attached questionnaires and capability statements for acquisition planning purposes. The following outline is recommended (5-page limit): 1) Company name, address, UEI (SAM), GSA contract # 2) A statement of capability which demonstrates the ability to perform this requirement. 3) Recent and relevant past performance information (Note: Prior government contract work is not required to submit a response.) USDA reserves the right to determine if a small business set-aside is appropriate based upon the capability information provided in response to this notice, and other pertinent information gathered by the contracting officer. Respondents should ensure the information provided is detailed, current, accurate, and complete. Please submit capability statements by email to Kathy Melby, Kathleen.melby@usda.gov, no later than November 30, 2026. This notice does not constitute a solicitation. This invitation for capability statements is for planning purposes only. The acquisition strategy for this proposed project has not yet been determined. Response to this notice is strictly voluntary. The Government will not reimburse any party for its participation in this effort. Information submitted in response to this notice is subject to disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act. Respondents are advised that the Government is under no obligation to acknowledge or provide feedback with respect to any information submitted under this notice.

title: 56 CS FOC to Flightline and Wx Equipment, Luke AFB
description: FINAL EXTENSION: Proposals are due no later than 30 November at 1300. NO ADDITIONAL EXTENSIONS WILL BE PROVIDED. Responses to Site Visit Q&A will be posted by 13 November 2026 at 1300 Arizona Time. The Government intends to hold a site visit for subject requirement on 4 November 2026 at 0900 AM. Below you will find the instructions and required documents to attend. Only SBA Certified Women Owned Small-Businesses are eligible for this requirement. **THIS IS THE ONLY DATE AND TIME FOR THE SITE VISIT, REQUESTS TO MAKE ANY CHANGES WILL BE DENIED** Attendance will be limited to 2 representatives for each contractor. To attend please provide the attached template (Site Visit Base Access_Template) completed with the below information, to rachel.tilley.1@us.af.mil, no later than 26 October 2026 at 1500 Arizona Time. Required Info: Last Name, First Name, DOB, US Citizen, License or ID#, State of Issue, Last 4 SSN To access the installation, the attendee will be required to have a REAL ID or Government Issued Passport. When submitting the above information, please include a copy of the form of ID to allow for Security Forces to verify if it meets the requirements. **QUESTIONS ARE DUE NO LATER THAN COB 22 OCTOBER 2026 at 1500 AZ time** ***FINALIZED Q&A Document will be posted with answers no later than 26 October 2026*** This SOW defines the requirement for the Contractor to Engineer, Furnish, Install and Test (EFI&T) new 12-Strand (St), Single Mode (SM) Fiber Optic Cable (FOC) from Radar Approach Control (RAPCON, B979) to Air Traffic Control Tower (ATCT, B998), Base Operation (Ops)B453), Command Post (CP, B11), Localizer (B1375), Glide Slope (GS, B1056), Tactical Air Navigation (TACAN, B1049), Ground Antenna Transmit and Receive (GATR, B1040), Glide Slope (B1081 and Localizer (B1059). Also, 12-St SM FOC from Base Ops (B453) to Primary and Secondary Automatic Meteorological Station (FMQ-19s). The work will be performed at Luke AFB AZ by using new and existing Manhole/Handhole Duct System. Some portion of the cable route/path will be Direct Buried. The Contractor shall provide all equipment, tools, materials, supplies, transportation, labor, supervision, management, and other incidentals necessary to meet the requirements as stated in this SOW. All equipment, supplies, or materials provided shall be new and not refurbished. No equipment, supplies, or material will be provided by the government. All materials used in this SOW must be rust-proof and corrosion-resistant, due to the nature of the environment. See attached Solicitation and supporting documents for additional information.

title: J041--VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS) Recurring Maintenance for Metasys Building Automation System and four (4) YORK Chillers
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS ONLY Building Automation System (BAS) and YORK Chiller Maintenance Services THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION, REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ), OR REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP). All information contained in this Sources Sought Announcement is preliminary, as well as subject to modification, and is in no way binding on the Government. The Government will not pay for any information submitted in response to this request. The information requested will be used solely within the Department of Veterans Affairs to facilitate decision making and will not be disclosed outside of the Government. The determination of a procurement strategy, based upon the comments submitted in response to this Sources Sought Announcement, is solely within the discretion of the Government. Inquiries will only be accepted in writing via email to Marc.Torres@va.gov on or before November 30, 2026, by 1:00 PM PST. Notice Type:� Sources Sought NAICS Code:� 811310 Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance Product Service Code (PSC):� J041 Maintenance, Repair, and Rebuilding of Equipment Refrigeration, Air Conditioning, and Air Circulating Equipment Place of Performance:� VA Long Beach Healthcare System, 5901 East 7th Street, Long Beach, CA 90822 Anticipated Period of Performance:� December 5, 2026, through December 4, 2031 (Base Year and Four Option Years) Response Deadline:� November 30, 2026, 1:00 PM PST 1. DESCRIPTION The Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Long Beach Healthcare System (VALBHS)� is conducting market research to identify qualified businesses capable of providing comprehensive preventive maintenance, repair, software maintenance, commissioning, and technical support services for the facility s existing Johnson Controls Metasys Building Automation System (BAS) and four YORK centrifugal chillers. The purpose of this notice is to determine the availability and capability of potential sources, including small businesses and eligible Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSBs) and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs), to perform the required services. Information obtained through this notice will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition strategy. 2. REQUIREMENT The VA Long Beach Healthcare System requires comprehensive maintenance and technical support services for its existing Johnson Controls Metasys BAS and four YORK centrifugal chillers. The contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, supervision, equipment, tools, materials, replacement parts, technical expertise, and other resources required to perform preventive maintenance, inspections, troubleshooting, repairs, software support, and emergency services. The anticipated scope of work includes, but is not limited to: Existing Proprietary System Environment The required services shall be performed on the Government s existing Johnson Controls Metasys Building Automation System and associated YORK centrifugal chillers. The installed Metasys system monitors and controls critical and non-critical mechanical equipment, including temperature, humidity, pressure, critical alarms, and equipment notifications supporting healthcare operations. The YORK chillers are integrated with and controlled through the existing Metasys system. The Government is not seeking replacement of the existing Metasys system. Any respondent must demonstrate that it possesses, or will possess before performance begins, the legal authority, technical capability, manufacturer-level access, qualified personnel, and proprietary resources necessary to perform the complete requirement on the installed system without loss of functionality, interruption of critical facility operations, compromise of cybersecurity, or invalidation of applicable warranties. At a minimum, the contractor must have the capability and legal authority to: Access, diagnose, maintain, program, configure, modify, and restore the installed Metasys system and its databases, controllers, field devices, sensors, interfaces, and associated components. Use all required proprietary or manufacturer-controlled Metasys software, service applications, programming tools, diagnostic tools, passwords, credentials, licenses, firmware, technical documentation, and update repositories. Obtain and install current, authorized Metasys software updates, firmware updates, security patches, hot fixes, and compatible replacement components throughout the period of performance. Service legacy Metasys controllers, sensors, and field devices currently installed at the facility, including equipment that may no longer be commercially available through ordinary distribution channels. Maintain full interoperability between the Metasys system, YORK chillers, mechanical equipment, alarms, operator workstations, servers, databases, communications networks, and existing control sequences. Perform work without disabling, bypassing, or degrading existing safety functions, environmental controls, monitoring capabilities, alarms, notifications, cybersecurity controls, or system integrations. Preserve all applicable equipment, software, and system warranties and avoid unauthorized system changes that could impair warranty coverage. Provide manufacturer-authorized or equivalently qualified technicians trained and experienced in the installed Metasys architecture and YORK centrifugal chillers. Coordinate software changes and security-patch activities with Government facility and information-technology personnel to avoid introducing cybersecurity vulnerabilities or disrupting critical healthcare operations. Obtain authorized original equipment manufacturer replacement parts and components necessary to maintain system compatibility and functionality. General familiarity with commercial building automation systems, experience with unrelated BAS platforms, or reliance on reverse-engineered, unlicensed, unauthorized, or unsupported software and tools will not, by itself, demonstrate capability to satisfy this requirement. Building Automation System Maintenance Scheduled preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of existing BAS equipment. Programming, calibration, and replacement of controllers, sensors, and associated components. Software maintenance, firmware updates, security patches, and database backups. Continuous commissioning, retro commissioning, fault detection, and system optimization. Energy management monitoring, reporting, and technical support. Recurring on-site BAS maintenance and technical services. Monthly room pressure monitoring and associated reporting. YORK Chiller Maintenance Preventive maintenance and operational inspections of four existing YORK centrifugal chillers. Scheduled operational and comprehensive maintenance visits. Equipment testing, inspections, lubrication, oil analysis, and applicable refrigerant services. Troubleshooting, repairs, and replacement of defective components. Technical support and emergency maintenance services in accordance with applicable equipment coverage requirements. Emergency Services and Reporting Emergency telephone support and on-site response capabilities. Maintenance documentation and service reporting. Coordination with designated Government personnel to minimize disruptions to facility operations. The contractor must demonstrate the ability to maintain the existing equipment and associated software while preserving applicable warranties and ensuring compatibility with the installed systems. 3.
