title: Long-Term Storage and Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) Services for Government-Owned Microelectronics
description: 1. Scope of Requirement DLA Weapons Support is conducting market research to identify potential sources capable of providing comprehensive Vendor-Managed Inventory (VMI) storage, management, packaging, and distribution (including packaging and shipping to third party integrator) for Government-Owned, serialized microcircuits. Management of inventory includes execution of full suite of Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) ANSI X.12 transactions and maintenance of data in the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE), including the Government Furnished Property (GFP) Module and/or Item Unique Identification (IUID) Registry. Management also includes delivering Contract Data Requirement List items such as annual inventory reports and inventory management plans. All hardware to be stored and managed is 100% manufactured and has been inspected, accepted, and is owned by the Government. The contemplated effort is strictly for logistics and warehousing services; no manufacturing, specialized electrical acceptance testing, or original design technical data packages (TDPs) are involved. DLA is contemplating firm fixed price contracts with a one year base period and up to eight one-year option periods. Beginning date for base period is TBD, and contract price structure is subject to change. 2. Key Technical & Operational Requirements Vendor Managed Inventory service includes, but is not limited to, entering the Government property into the Contractor�s inventory management system; storing these items in a secure location to prevent their accidental loss, theft, or tampering; transferring these items from inventory to fill authorized requests, and generating the necessary inventory reports in accordance with established DLA VMI practices. Delivery of an inventory management plan in accordance with FAR 52.245-1, to include quality control, subject to approval by DLA. Inventory plan and management system must be capable of accounting for assets by serial number or unique item identifier (UII, as defined by DFARS 252.211-7003) from acceptance to transfer to using entity. Capability to maintain, monitor, and certify long-term storage environments within contractor owned facility until material is transferred out of VMI. Storage must be specifically designed to prevent oxidation and moisture-induced degradation of microcircuits in accordance with GEIA-STD-0003A. Storage duration is to be determined. Requirement may include packaging, handling, and transportation for shipments to the next higher assembly (NHA) integrator. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION MULTI-SOURCE PNT UE 1.0 GENERAL INFORMATION This Request for Information (RFI) is issued solely for information and planning purposes (market research). This RFI does not constitute a solicitation (Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotations (RFQ)) or a promise to issue a solicitation in the future. This RFI does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. Furthermore, the Government is not, at this time, seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Respondents are advised the Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this RFI. All costs associated with responding to this RFI will be solely at the responding party�s expense. Not responding to this RFI does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if any is issued. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. Due to the operational sensitivity of the Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) missions, any future acquisition resulting from this market research will require strict adherence to Department of War (DoW) and Department of Defense (DoD) security, cybersecurity, and supply chain integrity standards. Consequently, while direct responses to this RFI must remain entirely unclassified (reach out to the government contacts below for information on classified submissions), respondents are required to demonstrate their organizational posture regarding facility clearances, information safeguarding, and National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) supply chain compliance. For the purposes of this market research, the anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for manufacturing global positioning systems (GPS) and related equipment is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing) with a Small Business Size Standard of $44.0 Million, and the primary Product Service Code (PSC) for Global Positioning Systems (GPS) hardware is 5825 (Radio Navigation Equipment, Except Airborne). For specialized, airborne GPS or radar navigation, the code is typically 5826. System-level R&D and engineering services for GPS are usually categorized under codes like R425 (Engineering Services) or AC13 (R&D�Defense System: Electronics). 2.0 BACKGROUND With advances in autonomous systems and guided munitions, the force that can best synchronize its activities at a single point in time and space wields a potent strategic advantage. In the future operating environment, therefore, the Joint Force will increasingly depend on resilient, reliable, and precise position, navigation, and timing (PNT) data to execute combat operations. As such, the Space Force is required to deliver global continuous coverage with stringent civil and military position and timing requirements to assure safety and mission success. This includes at least 88% of the constellation being operationally available more than 98% of the time. Likewise, a thinking adversary will make focused and deliberate efforts to deny access to this capability, leveraging a growing suite of threats including electromagnetic weapons, cyberspace attacks, and kinetic weapons. The challenge today is that, while satellite navigation (SATNAV) through the Global Positioning System (GPS) is foundational to U.S. military operations, critical infrastructure, and global commerce, the current architecture must adapt to evolving jamming and spoofing threats. Additionally, the space and ground segments must be modernized and hardened against physical attack. To build readiness for the future operating environment, therefore, the Space Force will pursue a comprehensive navigation warfare (NAVWAR) strategy that emphasizes resilience, technology modernization, modularity, adaptability, and flexibility. Specifically, it will adopt an open hybrid approach to SATNAV architecture that weighs inputs from diverse sources according to user need, generating a more dependable capability that can withstand adversary action while enabling faster upgrade cycles to enable PNT capabilities. The NAVWAR Objective Force pursues the development and deployment of several key capabilities to advance the SATNAV architecture. One of those elements is User Segment. To make best use of diversified PNT sources, the Space Force will enable a transition to a Multi-Source PNT user equipment (UE) reference architecture that incorporates Modular Open System Architectures (MOSA) and an onboard fusion engine to integrate all available data at the user level. The key enabler of the NAVWAR Objective Force is continued Joint Force investment in Multi-Source PNT UE that utilizes both traditional and new PNT sources. This equipment is foundational to a user�s ability to devise and execute a NAVWAR PACE (i.e., Primary / Alternate / Contingency / Emergency) Plan in degraded or denied environments. While legacy signals are expected to remain supported for civil and public functions, they are increasingly less effective in the contested environment. The military-specific M-Code is available today, while the PNT modernization signals are projected to be available by 2035. 3.0 OBJECTIVE, DESIRED CAPABILITIES AND CHARACTERISTICS This Request for Information (RFI) is focused on obtaining access to analytical information on industrial capabilities in Multi-Source PNT UE the NAVWAR Objective Force. Interests include the following: Multi-Source PNT UE for Terrestrial Users on various military platforms Disadvantaged user High value military assets MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Space Service Volume Multi-Source PNT UE (various orbits) Small satellite users Large satellite users MOSA Signals supported (M-code, CA, commercial), etc Interest is in technical details that can be incorporated into technical analysis to support Space Warfighting Analysis Center, Technology and Emerging Concept Assessments performed during Force Designs. This RFI is being executed in cooperation with the Space Warfighting Analysis Center (SWAC). 4.0 SECURITY, CYBERSECURITY AND SUPPLY CHAIN REQUIREMENTS The secure nature of this requirement dictates adherence to stringent Department of War (DoW) / Department of Defense (DoD) security protocols. While direct responses to this RFI must remain unclassified, respondents shall address their current capabilities and compliance regarding the following security domains: a. Facility and Personnel Security Clearances Given the operational nature of Multi-Source PNT UE and the potential for integration with multiple military architectures, e?orts will likely require access to classified information and systems. Respondents must state their current Facility Clearance Level (FCL) (e.g., None, Secret, Top Secret) and classified safeguarding capabilities. Respondents should confirm their capacity to provide appropriately cleared personnel (Personnel Security Clearances - PCL) and facility infrastructure to support secure development, testing, and operations. Please indicate your facility's current capability and experience in handling, storing, and integrating Communications Security (COMSEC) and Transmission Security (TRANSEC) materials. b. Cybersecurity and Information Safeguarding (CUI/CDI) The protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and Covered Defense Information (CDI) is critical to this effort. title: FSR and Engineering Support for C-27J aircraft
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE SYNOPSIS: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a sources sought notice only. This is NOT a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of commercially available products that may be of interest to the United States Coast Guard (USCG). The USCG, Aviation Logistics Center is conducting market research to determine repair sources described as follows: BACKGROUND: The USCG operates C-27J Maritime Patrol Aircraft. These Maritime Patrol Aircraft (MPA) operate differently from general aviation in support of USCG search and rescue missions, as well as surveillance and reconnaissance missions. The USCG C-27J missions require frequent operation at lower altitudes and in salt-laden environments. These environments accelerate corrosion on airframe structures, engines and components of the aircraft. The aircraft and its components are inspected by USCG personnel In Accordance With (IAW) the Original Equipment Manufacturer�s (OEM) periodic requirements and in conjunction with the USCG's specialized Asset Computerized Maintenance System (ACMS). The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of any commercially available vendors that may be of interest to the USCG. This notice is to assist the USCG in determining the potential sources capable of procurement for the services listed below. The Engine OEM is Rolls Royce Corporation who retains proprietary data rights. SERVICES: Field Service Representative services in support of C-27J aircraft. Program Manager/Engineering services in support of C-27 aircraft. REPLIES: Responses to this notice should include company name, address, and telephone number, point of contact (POC), details on company quality systems and include documentation that provides traceability to the OEM for each part, complete product details, brochures, etc., which will allow the USCG to understand your product, configurations, auxiliary equipment and options. Please state the approximate lead-time for acquiring your product and the details and terms of any standard warranty included with the product. Responses can be for all or for a few of the part numbers listed. Please provide the details and terms of any standard warranty included with the product. Please respond to the following questions: (1) Is your business a large or small business and how many employees? (2) If small, does your firm qualify as a small, emergent business, or a small, disadvantaged business? (3) If disadvantaged, specify under which disadvantaged group and is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? (4) Is your firm a certified hub zone firm? (5) Is your firm a woman-owned or operated business? (6) Is your firm a certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned? (7) Is your product listed on a GSA schedule? (8) Do you have other government agencies using the product, and if so which agencies, POCs and contract numbers? (9) If possible, any POCs for civilian users for general usage of product questions. After the review of the responses to this sources sought announcement, and if the USCG still plans to proceed with the acquisition, a solicitation announcement will be published on the SAM.GOV website. Insert "70Z03827IW0000001 Response" in the subject line of the email. After review of the responses to this sources sought announcement, and if the USCG decides to proceed with an acquisition, a solicitation announcement will be published on the SAM.GOV website. Again, this is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this sources notice shall be emailed to dane.w.hobbs@uscg.mil. TELEPHONE RESPONSES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. Responses must be received no later than 30 November 2026 at 4:00PM EST. Firms responding to this announcement that fail to provide all of the required information cannot be used to help the USCG make the appropriate acquisition decisions which is the intent of this sources sought notice. This notice is to assist the USCG in identifying potential sources only. All firms responding to this sources sought notice are advised that their response to this notice is not a request to be considered for a contract award. All interested parties must respond to any subsequent solicitation announcement separately from the responses to this announcement. Responses to this sources sought notice are NOT a request to be added to a prospective offerors list or to receive a copy of the solicitation. THE GOVERNMENT DOES NOT INTEND TO AWARD A CONTRACT ON THE BASIS OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE OR TO OTHERWISE PAY FOR THE INFORMATION SOLICITED. This request for information is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered as an Invitation for Bid (IFB), Request for Quotation (RFQ), or Request for Proposal (RFP), or as an obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services. Your responses to this sources sought notice will be treated as informational only. No entitlement to payment or direct or indirect costs or charges by the Government will arise as a result of contractor submission of responses to this sources sought notice or Government use of such information. The Government reserves the right to reject, in whole or part, any contractor input resulting from this sources sought notice. The information resulting from this sources sought notice may be included in one or more RFP�s, which may be released via the SAM.GOV portal.

title: Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC)
description: This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information (RFI) in attempt to determine local vendor capability/identify potential sources at Joint Base Anacostia Bolling (JBAB), DC 20032 and Andrews AFB, MD 20762 in accordance with RFO Part 10, Market Research. PLEASE NOTE - No reimbursement will be made for any costs associated with providing information in response to this synopsis or any follow up information requests. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SYNOPSIS. The purpose of this Sources Sought/RFI is to conduct market research for planning purposes to determine if responsible sources exist and to assist in determining if future efforts can be solicited on a competitive basis. This sources sought/RFI is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Description The 11th Contracting Squadron is publicizing this SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE in order to gather industry interest and information with respect to a potential Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Design-Build, Progressive Design-Build, Accelerated Design-Build, Design-Bid-Build Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) program. The government is seeking to identify qualified, experienced, and interested potential businesses capable of performing the type of work as described herein. The MACC provides a vehicle for execution of a broad range of maintenance; repair and minor/complex construction. For the purpose of this Request for Information (RFI), the work to be performed under the MACC will be within the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) codes as follows: 236210 ($45M Size Standard). Contractors will be expected to accomplish a wide variety of individual construction projects, including design/progressive design build (ranging from concept up to full 100% design), renovation, and additions/upgrades, along with specific work in hazardous material survey/abatement, heating/ventilation/air conditioning, electrical, mechanical, and other major trades. In-house design capability or ready access to design capability is a must for projects under the MACC. Description of the work will be identified in each individual task order. Individual task orders may range from $350,000 to $50,000,000. The program value is Not-to-Exceed $900,000,000 over a ten-year period. This acquisition is being considered as a 100% competitive 8(a) set-aside. All interested parties are invited to respond and prospective contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database at http://www.sam/gov/ before award of a government contract; failure to register in the SAM database will cause your firm to be ineligible for any future award. Any subsequent RFP will include a seed project that will be used to rate offeror's capabilities to determine basic contract awardees. The highest rated awardee will also receive award of the seed project. All other successful contract awardees are guaranteed a minimum of $2,500 during the first task order only. The government will compete future individual requirements with all of the awardees. The government anticipates an award of up to ten (10) contracts. The government will evaluate offers utilizing the best value source selection procedures described in the Federal Acquisition Regulation (RFO FAR Part 15), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS 215), and DoD Source Selection Procedures. If your firm has an interest in proposing on a future requirement as described above, please prepare a Capability Statement with details as follows: 1. Company name, address, point of contact (POC), telephone and email address of POC, CAGE Code, DUNS number. 2. Company's business size, to include the number of employees, number of years in the construction industry, and average annual gross revenue for the last three fiscal years. 3. Socioeconomic status, (e.g., SBA Certified 8(a) Program Participant). 4. Potential teaming arrangements and delineation between the work that will be accomplished by the prime and the work accomplished by the teaming partner(s). Note: For general and heavy construction 15% of the cost of the contract, not including the cost of materials, must be performed by the prime contractor with its own employees. 5. Representation of ability to execute a broad range of maintenance, repair, and construction of real property (i.e. carpentry, excavation, interior renovation, exterior renovation, electrical, plumbing, painting, paving, roofing, demolition, masonry, hazardous material survey/abatement, and HVAC) from an on-the-shelf design, or a design provided in-house or through subcontract designers (including design ranging from concept to full 100% design). Identify specialty construction trades performed by prime company employees, if any, as well as experience in delivering multi-trade design/build projects. 6. In-house Architect-Engineering capability, up to complete 100% design or ready access to design capability. Identify if you : 1) have in-house design capability; 2) have state certified Professional Engineers and/or registered Architects on staff ; 3) which A-E disciplines you have the ability to design in-house (Mechanical, Electrical, Structural, Fire Protection, etc.), and 4) or whether you subcontract all A-E services. 7. Surge capability to provide significant increase in support (e.g. rapidly identify, employ and equip resources) in the event of a government End of Fiscal Year (EOFY) or Economic surge in number, size or complexity of projects. 8. Past/Current performance for projects within the last 3 years where your firm was the Prime Contractor, to include: a. Contract identification number(s) b. Title and a brief summary of the project requirements c. Contracting Agency or firm (Government or commercial) d. Value of contracts at award and completion to include the number/value of modifications e. Type of contract (fixed price, cost reimbursement, labor hour, etc.) f. Design-Build or Bid-Build (looking for representation of each) g. Percentage of work done as the Prime Contractor 9. Largest multi-trade project your company has successfully completed, to include value, name and location of client, date completed, and whether the project was renovation or new construction. 10. Identify bonding capacity and name(s) of surety(ies). 11. Provide recommendations of commercial practices the Government should consider implementing for this acquisition.

title: Vehicles Rental Service
description: The Embassy of the United States in Quito will establish Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for qualified vehicle rental service providers. These vehicles will be used to conduct daily operations; therefore, vehicles must be locally common. The U.S. Government intends to award a Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) to one or more responsible companies submitting an acceptable quotation with fair and reasonable prices. We intend to award a BPA based on initial quotations, without holding discussions, although we may hold discussions with companies if there is a need to do so. A BPA is an Agreement, not a contract, and neither party is bound by its terms and conditions. The Government is not obligated to purchase any definite amount under this BPA. If a need arises, an authorized representative of the Government may issue an order following the procedures outlined in the BPA. If the BPA holder accepts the order, then a binding contract between the Government and BPA holder will exist for that specific order. If the BPA-holder refuses to accept orders or furnish quotations in compliance with the terms of the Agreement, then it is likely that the Government will cancel the Agreement. If you are interested in participating in this solicitation, follow the instructions in Section 3 of the solicitation, complete the required portions of the attached document, and submit your proposal electronically to Quitoprocurement@state.gov making reference to "Quotation Enclosed � Vehicle Rental Services". title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFAs international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities. NETSAFAs international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: NETSAFA International Training Center Support
description: See the Attached Solicitation, PWS and other Solicitation related attachments. This opportunity is a 100% Small-business set-aside CPFF Task Order under Seaport NxG. The Naval Education and Training Security Assistance Field Activity (NETSAFA), Pensacola, Florida, requires educational and training services, engineering and technical services, logistics, administration, management assistance, consulting and facilitation services, and transportation support services, training liaison, special mission personnel, and curriculum development. These services may be required in various locations in the U.S. or in foreign countries and may include support to foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs) under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP)/Security Assistance Training Program (SATP). The PSC code for this action is U099 Education/Training-Other associated with NAICS code 541330 under the Knowledge Based Services Taxonomy of services. NETSAFA supports international training in all warfare areas and at all levels of training for foreign countries. This is accomplished by staffing, operating, and managing international training support provided at NETSAFA's international training sites. The training sites are located in the NETASAFA International Training Center (NITC) located at Naval Air Station (NAS) Pensacola, Florida and NAS Whiting Field, Milton, Florida, and NITC Detachment Whiting Field, Milton, Florida. These sites are outfitted with computer training facilities, classrooms, and equipment needed to teach courses. They provide training and training support services in Navy activities such as government-owned contractor operating facilities.NETSAFA's international training sites are currently operational and have established curriculum. The training and other services required by this Performance Work Statement (PWS) are currently centered in four categories: General Training Programs, Aviation Training Programs, Mobile Training Teams (MTTs), and Mobile Education Teams (METs). Additionally, support will be required to meet emerging requirements in support of the SCETP/SATP. The instant requirement is for services associated with the international requirement of the United States and the foreign countries participating in the SCETP/SATP for a 12-month base period of performance beginning 01 March 2027 through 29 February 2028, with four (4) consecutive 12-month option periods pursuant to FAR 52.217-9, and a 6-month option period pursuant to FAR 52.217-8. The contractor will be required to periodically perform these services in various locations in the U.S. and may be required to perform these services in foreign countries. If support is needed in a foreign country, the contractor may be required to support foreign governments with formal and informal schools and courses, mobile training teams, and mobile education teams under the auspices of the Security Cooperation Education Training Program (SCETP) /Security Assistance Training Program (SATP).

title: Army Enterprise HVAC Modernization and Lifecycle Sustainment Maintenance
description: ***************START OF 16 NOV UPDATE*************** The CSO Q&A file is updated/replaced at the attached herein to provide government responses/clarity to all interested parties. NOTE: there has been NO change to government responses from the previously posted Q&A (i.e., Q1-Q4). The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 16 NOV UPDATE****************** ***************START OF 10 NOV UPDATE*************** The government has provided a list of Army Enterprise Garrison HVAC projects identified as potential projects over the FY27-31 CSO projected project period. Please note these potential projects have NOT been approved or funded at this time. Potential Offerors may utilize this data as deemed appropriate in preparation of Solution Briefs/White Papers. It is anticipated the government will update and refine this data, as applicable, throughout the CSO acquisition process and share updates with industry, as appropriate. The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 10 NOV UPDATE****************** ***************START OF 06 NOV UPDATE*************** A CSO Question & Answer (Q&A) file is attached herein to provide government responses/clarity to all interested parties. Additionally, CSO Amendment 0002 (A002) has been issued/posted herein to clarify requirements at para. 3.2.1 and to require MICC POC be placed on copy when industry questions are submitted to the AoI POC. The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 06 NOV UPDATE****************** ***************START OF 02 NOV UPDATE*************** CSO Amendment 0001 (A001), to provide the incorporated Attachment 3, is posted herein. The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 02 NOV UPDATE****************** The U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), on behalf of the U.S. Army Installation Management Command (IMCOM), is seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide an Army Enterprise Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Modernization & Lifecycle Sustainment Maintenance Plan, and associated project management of the plan throughout the project period, Fiscal Year (FY) FY27-FY31. This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will utilize a solicitation process authorized by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under this CSO, the Department of War (DoW) will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide a solution for Army Enterprise HVAC modernization and lifecycle sustainment maintenance. CSO procedures provide a streamlined acquisition process and simplified contract terms resulting in RFO FAR-based contracts awarded under RFO FAR Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures. Both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors may be awarded contracts under this CSO. Under a CSO DoW contracting (or agreement) officers may competitively select proposals received in response to a general competitive solicitation, similar to a broad agency announcement, based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject matter experts. While this is a complete CSO as detailed herein, the MICC reserves the right to pursue alternative contracting methods as a result of Offeror responses to Phase 1 requirements herein and continued government analysis. For example, the government may elect to pursue a solution via Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). If this, or any other change occurs, the public will be notified via sam.gov posting. Industry parties interested in responding to this CSO shall request access to Attachments 1 and 2 by submitting justification/reason for access as instructed in this sam.gov post. The MICC team will receive notification of the request, review, and release, as appropriate, within one business day. Finally, the government anticipates hosting a future industry conference. Accordingly, industry is encouraged to monitor this sam.gov posting for updates, to include the date, time, and location of any such event.

Under this CSO, the Department of War (DoW) will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide a solution for Army Enterprise HVAC modernization and lifecycle sustainment maintenance. Under a CSO DoW contracting (or agreement) officers may competitively select proposals received in response to a general competitive solicitation, similar to a broad agency announcement, based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject matter experts. title: AMS Designated Laboratory Meat Testing Services (ADL)
description: Amendment A01 Posted 11/18/2026. The purpose of this amendment is to answer questions received in response to the solicitation identified in Block 9A and to make changes to the SF-1449/solicitation/performance work statement and other attachments. The solicitation due date has been extended to November 30, 2026, at 4:30 p.m CST. Offerors must acknowledge this amendment and any other amendment when submitting their proposal and SF-1449. The solicitation and performance work statement has been updated in multiple sections, please make sure to read them in their entirety. Please see the questions and answers document that has been added to the attachment section. All proposals should be sent to Daniel Moore via email at daniel.moore@usda.gov The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS) is issuing Solicitation 12?1NTS?26?R?0002 to obtain proposals from responsible, accredited analytical laboratories to perform microbiological and fat testing in support of AMS meat, poultry, egg, and aquatic product procurement programs. This requirement establishes AMS Designated Laboratories (ADLs) responsible for conducting all required microbiological and chemical analyses on samples submitted by AMS vendors, ensuring compliance with Federal Purchase Program Specifications (FPPS) and supporting food safety and quality verification efforts. AMS intends to award an Indefinite Delivery/Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) firm?fixed?price contract, consisting of a Base Period and up to four option periods, covering performance from April 1, 2027 through March 31, 2032. Offerors must be fully capable of meeting all technical, accreditation, reporting, and quality assurance requirements outlined in the Statement of Work (SOW) and must maintain ISO/IEC 17025 accreditation for all applicable microbiological and chemical test methods throughout the contract term. Offerors are required to submit a complete proposal package in accordance with Section E of the solicitation, including all technical, management, past performance, and pricing components, as well as a properly completed and signed SF?1449. Offerors must ensure all requirements, instructions, and submission details�such as WBSCM electronic submission processes�are fully reviewed and followed. Incomplete proposals may not be considered for award. Key expectations under this solicitation include: � Performance of all required microbiological and fat analyses using approved methods (FSIS MLG, AOAC, AOCS, or AMS?approved alternatives). � Comprehensive sample preparation, receipt, testing, reporting, and data management in accordance with AMS SOW requirements. � Timely reporting of results, including notification of presumptive or confirmed pathogen positives to AMS, FSIS, and vendors. � Secure handling and management of proprietary AMS data. � Full compliance with FAR, AGAR, and USDA?specific contract clauses incorporated into the solicitation. Prospective offerors are strongly encouraged to read the entire solicitation package, including the SOW, exhibits, and all referenced clauses, to ensure a complete and conforming submission.

The Phase 1 response date remains unchanged, 30 Nov 2026, 4:30PM EST. ***************END OF 02 NOV UPDATE****************** The U.S. Army Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC), on behalf of the U.S. Army Installation Management Command (IMCOM), is seeking innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide an Army Enterprise Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Modernization & Lifecycle Sustainment Maintenance Plan, and associated project management of the plan throughout the project period, Fiscal Year (FY) FY27-FY31. This Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) will utilize a solicitation process authorized by Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) DFARS Subpart 212.70. Under this CSO, the Department of War (DoW) will be allowed to competitively procure innovative commercial technologies, products and/or services that will provide a solution for Army Enterprise HVAC modernization and lifecycle sustainment maintenance. CSO procedures provide a streamlined acquisition process and simplified contract terms resulting in RFO FAR-based contracts awarded under RFO FAR Part 12 Commercial Item Procedures. Both traditional and non-traditional defense contractors may be awarded contracts under this CSO. Under a CSO DoW contracting (or agreement) officers may competitively select proposals received in response to a general competitive solicitation, similar to a broad agency announcement, based on a review of proposals by scientific, technological, or other subject matter experts. While this is a complete CSO as detailed herein, the MICC reserves the right to pursue alternative contracting methods as a result of Offeror responses to Phase 1 requirements herein and continued government analysis. For example, the government may elect to pursue a solution via Other Transaction Agreement (OTA). If this, or any other change occurs, the public will be notified via sam.gov posting. Industry parties interested in responding to this CSO shall request access to Attachments 1 and 2 by submitting justification/reason for access as instructed in this sam.gov post. The MICC team will receive notification of the request, review, and release, as appropriate, within one business day. Finally, the government anticipates hosting a future industry conference. Accordingly, industry is encouraged to monitor this sam.gov posting for updates, to include the date, time, and location of any such event.

title: Finland – Repair and maintenance services of machinery – Framework agreement for Shop Inspection, Repair and Testing Services for Pratt & Whitney and Rolls-Royce gas generators
description: The object of the procurement is a framework contract arrangement for shop inspection, repair, and engine testing services for the Pratt & Whitney and Rolls-Royce gas generators utilized at the reserve power plants owned and operated by Fingrid Oyj in Finland. The object of the procurement is divided into two (2) parts: Part 1: Shop inspection, repair, and engine testing services for the Pratt & Whitney JT4 and GG4 gas generators 2027 - 2031. Part 2: Shop inspection, repair, and engine testing services for the Rolls-Royce Avon gas generators 2027 - 2031. Both parts 1 and 2 are framework contract arrangements and the client aims to sign a framework contract within each part with all suppliers who fulfil the minimum requirements set in this invitation to participate. A supplier may apply for participation in more than one part. If less than two (2) suppliers are qualified for either part the client may opt to not sign a contract with any suppliers within this part. The services shall be ordered on as needed basis through setting up mini-competitions with the selected suppliers within each part. The supplier providing the overall most economically advantageous tender in the mini-competition shall be chosen. The scope of work for each mini-competition shall vary, but will typically include the following services: 1. Receipt of work, inspection, documentation and compiling of an initial report; 2. Full disassembly, inspection and initial condition assessment and cost estimate for component repairs or replacements; 3. Required component repairs and replacements; 4. Re-assembly including all expendable items, single life items and consumables; 5. Engine testing, dispatch and documentation; 6. Preparation for shipment and packing in std. container The framework contract does not oblige Fingrid to purchase services from those suppliers admitted to the framework contract arrangement. The preliminary schedule for the procurement is: INVITATION TO PARTICIPATE This Invitation to Participate has been launched launched in November 2026. Interested parties are invited to send an application to Participate: Deadline to provide Application see IV.2.2. APPLICATIONS AND THEIR EVALUATION All candidates, who have submitted the application within the set deadline and who meet the minimum requirements set for the candidate’s eligibility will be selected to the negotiated procedure. INVITATION TO NEGOTIATE The candidates selected as tenderers shall be in receipt of an invitation to negotiate and preliminary schedule of negotiations, app. in January 2027. A preliminary Request to tender will also be enclosed to the Invitation to negotiate. NEGOTIATIONS The preliminary time for negotiations is during February 2027. Fingrid shall conduct negotiations separately and equally with each party. The purpose of the negotiations is to finalize the Request to tender. CALL FOR TENDER After the negotiations Fingrid shall send the Final Request to tender to the tenderers. Estimated time for this is in March 2027, and deadline of submission of tenders by the tenderers, approximately in April 2027. EVALUATION OF FINAL TENDERS AND CONTRACT AWARD Fingrid aim to finalize the procurement process during May 2027. Before evaluation of the submitted tenders, Fingrid shall verify that the tenders and the services tendered fulfill the requirements of the Request to tender. Tenders contrary to Request to tender shall be excluded from the comparison. The intention is to sign the frame work agreements during May 2027.

title: Spain – Structures and parts of structures – Fabricación, suministro, desmontaje y sustitución de chimeneas de escape de turbocompresores en las Estaciones de Compresión de Alcázar de San Juan, Sevilla, Algete y Almendralejo
description: El contrato tiene por objeto la ingeniería de detalle, fabricación, suministro, transporte, desmontaje de los equipos existentes, montaje, instalación, pruebas y puesta en servicio de cuatro chimeneas de evacuación de gases de escape asociadas a turbinas de gas: TC3 de Alcázar de San Juan, TC2 de Sevilla, TC1 de Algete y TC2 de Almendralejo. El alcance incluirá, como mínimo: verificaciones aerodinámicas, térmicas, mecánicas y estructurales; adaptación a las condiciones reales de operación; fabricación completa de las nuevas chimeneas y de sus elementos internos de atenuación acústica; suministro de revestimientos, aislamiento, chapas y soportes; desmontaje y retirada de las chimeneas existentes; montaje, inspecciones, ensayos y documentación final. La solución deberá cumplir la normativa UNE-EN e ISO aplicable, incluida ISO 21905 cuando proceda, y deberá garantizar la integridad estructural, la seguridad, el comportamiento acústico y la fiabilidad de las instalaciones.

title: SPN-50 FY27 EDM Contract
description: 1. INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command, (NAVAIR) Patuxent River, Maryland, Air Traffic Management Systems Program Office (PMA-213) intends to award a new contract to procure Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 AN/SPN-50 Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR)(V)3 Internal Research and Development (IRAD) system. 2.0 DISCLAIMER This synopsis is for informational purposes only. THIS NOTICE IS NOT A REQUEST FOR COMPETITIVE PROPOSALS. The government intends to negotiate the contract under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) (formerly known as 10 U.S.C. 2304(c)(1)), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.302-1, only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for the action described herein is 334511. 3.0 BACKGROUND The procurement of AN/SPN-50 Shipboard Air Traffic Radar (SATR)(V)3 Internal Research and Development (IRAD) system will serve as an Engineering Development Model (EDM) asset. The IRAD system will be utilized for environmental and qualification?testing.?This effort will require contractor support for the testing and installation. 4.0 INCUMBENT NAVAIR requires deliveries of AN/SPN-50 radars to remain on schedule for installation efforts on CVN, LHD, and LHA ships. Specialized skills are required for the production effort to meet the stringent schedule. The AN/SPN-50 includes integration of complex contractor developed software and hardware in conjunction with Government cooperation using organically developed algorithms for target processing. This system is specialized for operation with the AN/SYY-1 Display system, involving characterization of the system in their operational environment to ensure ship requirements are met. The Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) is the sole AN/SPN-50 designer, developer and manufacturer. The U.S. Navy did not procure the Technical Data Package (TDP) that would allow another source to produce the AN/SPN-50.

title: J061--Eaton Powerware System Replacement
description: 36C24127Q0030 UPS Eaton Powerware System Replacement - RFIs Does the VA require technicians performing quarterly and annual preventive maintenance to be individually factory-certified or authorized by Eaton? Due to the complex nature of the product and criticality - Yes Will documented experience and technical qualifications satisfy the qualification requirement for routine preventive maintenance? Prime Contractor does not require that; That portion can be filled through an Eaton Authorized Technician. Would a contractor be considered technically acceptable if it performs routine maintenance using qualified technicians and subcontracts manufacturer-restricted procedures and startup to Eaton? Since Eaton has discontinued the 93E product line, will the VA accept the current Eaton 93PM or another equivalent replacement system meeting the required performance specifications? Yes, See photos. The UPS is required to be able to go into maintenance Bypass and maintain power to the computer room during maintenance. What is the kVA rating of the existing unit? The SOW says "Model 80," but the replacement is specified at 60 kVA. Existing UPS is 80KVA. The goal is to replace-in- kind. The 60kVA was utilized as a basis of design. What are the existing input voltage and output voltage?
